absent: Per group inheritance selection and cloning policy for individual events
Pinning, reference counting and generation management for task and processor contexts
Rotation, scheduling and time accounting algorithms for event groups
Event removal, group detach and scheduling out mechanics
Scoped topology mapping and monitoring context migration mechanics
Monitoring device allocation and bus registration mechanics
Tracepoint, software and clock monitoring unit internals
Hardware slot query, configuration parsing and architectural install and removal
Breakpoint validation details and enable and disable propagation
Kernel counter creation, overflow handling and release mechanics
Control group switch and per task invocation mechanics
Deferred unwind invocation timing and execution context
Software hash lookup, reference lifecycle and read copy update reclamation
Constraint guard selection and global semaphore protection scope
Exception notification dispatch beyond registration priority
Exact memory layouts of task, context, event and processor control structures
Printk, power, module, DMA, debug and audit behaviors implied by dossier title but not shown here

findings.text: Task performance state preparation and parental inheritance during creation, with automatic teardown when inheritance reports failure, and immediate success when the creator holds no monitoring context.
Per processor performance context online and offline handling, including topology mask maintenance and migration plus remote teardown of remaining events, exposed for hotplug and reboot paths.

Early boot initialization of the performance subsystem covering identifier management, deferred unwinding, per processor state, core software and clock monitoring units, tracepoint support, current processor activation, reboot notification, breakpoint support and event caching with layout validation.

Readout of configured event description strings through device attributes, returning an empty result when no description is present, plus bus level discovery that instantiates missing device nodes for known monitoring units.

Hardware breakpoint lifecycle management including slot reservation and release, kernel and user registration, attribute modification with temporary deactivation, single release, usage query, and per processor wide registration with collective teardown.

Debugger oriented slot acquisition and release that refuse when constraint protection appears held and otherwise operate without holding the normal constraint guards while suppressing lock validation.
Registration of deferred unwinding callbacks by allocating a distinct bit position from a global mask and linking the work item for later invocation, failing when no positions remain.

Control group integration for performance monitoring providing state allocation and release, online notification, and migration handling that switches monitoring state on each moved task with preemption control.

Hardware breakpoint subsystem startup that prepares task lookup storage, obtains slot capacity, marks constraints ready, registers the breakpoint monitoring unit and subscribes to exception notifications.

When the creating task holds no performance context or its pinned context cannot be obtained, creation time inheritance completes successfully without touching the new task beyond its initial empty state.

A newly populated child context becomes linked as a clone only when some state was created and every parental group was inherited, pointing either at the ultimate ancestor when the parent is itself a clone or at the parent otherwise, capturing the matching generation and holding a reference while protected against concurrent unlinking.

Early per processor preparation establishes empty online tracking, initializes software event protection and lists, sideband and scheduling callback state, and per processor monitoring contexts with distinct lock identities, online status derived from tracking, and default heap storage.

Per processor software event hash storage is created on demand only while protected, when a positive user count exists but no table is yet published, using node local zeroed memory published through read copy update semantics.

Processor offline handling first updates global and scoped online tracking and migrates scoped monitoring contexts toward surviving peers before remotely scheduling out and detaching any remaining events, marking the processor offline only after those steps.

Boot processor setup populates every scope mask unconditionally when global tracking is still empty, while later processors add themselves only to scopes whose topology domain currently lacks representation, always ending marked globally online.

Control group monitoring state exists only when both the container object and its per processor information succeed allocation, is fully released on teardown, signals online entry, and moves tasks by invoking a per task switch routine.

Breakpoint slot capacity setup has a trivial always successful build and a full build that snapshots per type capacities then allocates per processor and global histograms, releasing all partial progress when any allocation fails.

Wide breakpoint creation either yields a per processor collection fully populated for every online processor or releases everything already created and returns an error carrier, while teardown tolerates empty slots and releases the collection.

Breakpoint event acceptance requires breakpoint typed configuration with available hardware capacity for its category and without branch sampling, reserves capacity before parsing, installs automatic release on destruction, and returns capacity when parsing fails.

Unwind callback registration starts from zeroed storage and succeeds exactly once per free mask position by claiming the lowest free bit, linking the entry and storing the handler, otherwise reporting resource exhaustion when the mask is full.

Task breakpoint lookup uses a resizable hash keyed by target identity with list linkage at a defined offset and automatic shrinking, gated by a readiness flag that becomes true only after slot initialization completes.
Reboot handling walks all online processors through the same offline path used by hotplug and reports successful notification handling.

Parental group inheritance holds the parental context mutex across both pinned and flexible walks, while the child requires no protection because it is neither visible by identifier nor eligible to run yet.

A processor status saving spin guard protects the rotation suppression flag around the flexible walk and also protects the child clone linkage update against concurrent interrupt driven rotation and unlinking.
Software event hash inspection and publication are serialized by a per processor mutex covering both the reference count test and the table install.
Global monitoring unit protection is acquired before any per processor context mutex during processor setup, teardown and bus discovery, with the inner mutex released before the outer.

Normal slot reservation and release execute under a per event constraint guard selected for the breakpoint, while a lock state query reports held status by inspecting a global processor semaphore in write mode or else a task guard or read mode.
Wide breakpoint population holds the processor set read guard across creation for all online processors, preventing topology changes mid walk.
Unwind mask search and update plus callback list linkage occur while holding the callback mutex through scoped acquisition.
Remote processor teardown holds the target context spin guard while scheduling out and while walking and detaching every event in group detach mode.
Control group migration disables preemption only around the per task monitoring switch invocation inside the per task helper.

Slot usage histogram stores one atomic counter per hardware slot, using inline fixed storage when build time capacity is known and dynamically allocated storage otherwise, with allocation sized from cached capacity and release returning the memory.
Per processor breakpoint accounting combines a count of processor pinned breakpoints with a histogram of task pinned usage, instantiated as a per processor array indexed by breakpoint category.
Global breakpoint state comprises per category processor pinned and task pinned histograms plus per category slot totals that become immutable after early initialization.

Breakpoint monitoring unit description binds software context numbering with lifecycle handlers for initialization, insertion, removal, starting, stopping and reading, where destruction automatically releases reserved capacity.
Control group subsystem description binds allocation, release, online and attach handlers and declares default hierarchy enablement plus threaded operation.
Reboot notification linkage uses minimal priority to run last, while breakpoint exception linkage uses maximal priority to run first.

Breakpoint events progress from validation and capacity reservation through insertion with optional stopped marking and sampling period seeding, then alternate between running and stopped markings, ending with architectural removal and automatic capacity release on destruction.

Per processor monitoring contexts move from early initialized but offline, to online after mask setup, remaining online across operation, then back to offline after mask clearing, migration and event detachment during teardown or reboot.

Slot handling moves from free to reserved before configuration parsing, returning to free when parsing fails or when explicit or automatic release occurs, with debugger paths using the same transitions without holding guards.

Breakpoint modification passes through deactivation using a local or global path selected by interrupt state and target affinity, then validation, then conditional reactivation only when the resulting configuration requests enablement.

Boot time entry establishes identifier storage, deferred unwinding, per processor state, core monitoring units, tracepoint support, current processor activation, reboot linkage, breakpoint support and event caching with layout checking.

Hotplug online, hotplug offline and reboot notification entries converge on shared mask and context helpers, with offline work delegated to a synchronous remote function on the target processor when events remain, alongside an empty offline variant for constrained builds.

Monitoring unit, control group, sysfs and exception handlers serve as subsystem callbacks for event lifecycle, group membership changes, attribute readout and fault notification rather than direct call targets.
Task creation entry prepares empty monitoring linkage and list state before attempting parental inheritance, ensuring a well defined child even when inheritance is skipped.
Walking flexible groups without suppressing rotation risks concurrent interrupt driven list mutation, so suppression must bracket the entire walk and only then be cleared.

Modifying a breakpoint while interrupts are disabled cannot use cross processor signaling, so it must use a direct local path and only when operating on the running task, otherwise a global deactivation path is required.

Debugger slot paths intentionally operate without constraint guards and with lock validation suppressed, so callers must first verify through the lock state query that no conflicting holder exists, otherwise they fail without side effects.

Partial failures during slot table setup, wide creation, software table creation and bus device creation require careful unwinding or continuation: slot setup frees everything, wide creation tears down all prior processors, software creation warns on allocation miss, and bus discovery warns yet reports overall success.

Usage reporting treats any processor pinned count or any task histogram entry as in use, but warns when global processor histograms show usage without matching per processor counts, indicating accounting skew.
Breakpoint release tolerates a null handle as a no operation, while wide teardown iterates over all possible processors rather than only online ones to cover sparse populations.
Mapped event control page places its data head sequence field at byte offset one thousand twenty four, enforced by a build time check during boot initialization.

Core monitoring units register under fixed names for software, processor clock, task clock and breakpoint operation, with software and breakpoint bound to their respective numeric families and clocks using negative one as untyped.
Reboot handling runs at the lowest integer priority and signals successful handling, while breakpoint fault handling runs at the largest positive thirty two bit priority to precede other observers.

Event insertion without an explicit start request leaves hardware state marked stopped, sampling events seed their last period from the configured sample interval, and start clears the stopped marking while stop restores it.
Scope mask maintenance iterates categories strictly between none and the maximum, using negative one to denote absence of a migration target and processor count as the bound for valid targets.
Control group integration declares implicit enablement on the default hierarchy and threaded mode operation as part of its subsystem identity.
